title: VPC quickcheck orchestrator: synthetic API readiness and model saturation sweep
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement an automated post-deploy 'quickcheck' orchestrator for Private (VPC) deployments that runs a short, deterministic suite of API readiness checks, lightweight model-load/saturation sweeps, and smoke tests immediately after Terraform apply and service rollout. The goal is to detect regressions in runtime binary, kernel selection, network ACLs, and model hotstart behavior before handing the deployment to customers or the next pipeline stage.
acceptance_criteria: A1: After a successful terraform apply for a private deployment, the orchestrator is invoked automatically (via CI hook) and returns a pass/fail status to the pipeline within 12 minutes for standard stacks.
A2: The suite validates API handshake, authentication, short-generation correctness (sanity prompts), and token-level latency thresholds: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 450ms under synthetic light-load profile.

A3: Model load sweep runs 3 quick scenarios (tiny, short, convo) that exercise KV cache warmup and detect OOM/slow kernel degradations; failures generate a ticket in Linear and prevent promotion to the next environment.
A4: Results and artifacts (logs, perf histograms, generated samples) are persisted to the deployment object's audit bucket and linked in the deployment record in Console within 30 minutes.
A5: Orchestrator is configurable by Terraform module (boolean flag) and controlled by a rollout feature flag; default for new private stacks is enabled.
A6: Security posture: orchestrator runs under least-privileged role (KMS read-only to fetch keys when needed) and does not write customer data to external telemetry endpoints.
A7: Automated retries/backoff: on transient infra failures (network/TLS), the orchestrator retries up to 2 times before marking as flaky; persistent failures create an incident playbook link.
A8: Unit/integration tests for Terraform modules and the runner are present in the repo and pass in CI.
implementation_steps: Step 1: Add quickcheck flag and orchestration hooks to modules/private-deploy/terraform/main.tf (module input: run_postdeploy_quickcheck=true by default).
Step 2: Create a lightweight check-runner service (k8s Job + helm chart) that accepts a deployment ID and runs the suite; reuse existing smoke-harness container base image and add new scenarios.

Step 3: Implement orchestration lambda in infra-ci that listens to deployment completed events and triggers the k8s Job via the cluster API; record run metadata to S3 and to Console via existing events API.

Step 4: Define three model scenarios (tiny-legacy, short-ll, convo-medium) that exercise different attention lengths and KV cache hits; parametrized in runner config files stored in repo under /infra/quickcheck/scenarios.
Step 5: Wire Terraform to create necessary service account, IAM bindings, and an S3 audit bucket path for run artifacts; ensure KMS key policies are limited to the runner.
Step 6: Add CI pipeline stage (private-deploy-quickcheck) that waits for orchestrator completion and evaluates pass criteria; failures block promotion and open ENG tickets with logs attached.
Step 7: Add metrics emission (prometheus) for run duration, p50/p95 latency, error ratio, kv-cache-warmup-time; create default Grafana dashboard panel and alert policy for >30% error rate.
Step 8: Document runbook and Create Confluence 'Private: Quickcheck Orchestrator' with troubleshooting steps and rollback guidance.
Step 9: Run staged rollout to internal e2e/private testbed, iterate on thresholds, then enable by default for new private deployments.
test_plan: Unit: Terraform module validation (tflint, terraform validate) and module-level plan tests in terratest.
Integration: Deploy to internal VPC testbed using terraform-nightly, assert orchestrator triggers and artifacts appear in S3; validate Console links and metadata.
Load-sanity: Run model saturation sweep with artificially throttled GPU to validate failure detection (simulate slow kernels and check p95 threshold alarms).
Chaos: Inject transient network failures in a controlled run to ensure retries/backoff work and flaky runs are marked correctly.
Regression: Add synthetic golden prompts and lexical checks to ensure output shape and structured-output fields are unchanged.
Security: Verify orchestrator role cannot access customer data paths and KMS operations limited to decrypt-only for runner secrets.
Smoke automation: Add nightly scheduled quickcheck against long-lived staging stack to detect drift and kernel regressions early.
rollout_notes: Phase 0: Feature branch + internal e2e cluster validation. Only runs when explicit flag enabled.
Phase 1: Canary enablement for 5% of private deployments via feature flag gate; monitor metrics and alerts for 72 hours.
Phase 2: Gradual ramp to 100% for new stacks after two successful canary windows; for existing stacks opt-in via stack update.

Rollback: If orchestrator causes pipeline slowdowns or false positives, disable feature flag and revert terraform changes creating the service account; PR will include a one-click revert shortcut in CI.
Monitoring: Dashboards and alerting included in release note; SRE on-call will watch the first 3 days and own immediate triage.
